newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bonds unmoved awaiting auction, depos up.
newsitem.headline: Greek bonds unmoved awaiting auction, depos up.

text.p: Greek depos were trading higher across-the-board as players sought funding for today's bond auction and forex forwards were little changed, dealers said.

Bonds were frozen, awaiting the auction of five-, seven- and 10-year bonds but dealers said demand for the bonds appeared to be low with investors having sustained losses in fixed coupon bonds lately, traders said.
Ecu/drachma was trading in the narrow 309.45/60 range and the mark was firmer against the drachma on a softer ecu/mark, traders said.
"Forex forwards are little changed but depos are up a tenth of a point in early dealings on funding for today's bond auction," said a dealer at a private bank.
Bonds and FRNs were stable, awaiting the auction of five-, seven-and 10-year bonds but demand appeared to be low, dealers said.

"Players who invested in fixed coupon bonds have been hurt by falling prices and this does not bode well for the auction," the dealer said. "I expect cut-off prices of 96 for the 10-year and seven-year bonds and 97.5 percent for the five-year bond."
The market showed greater interest for five-year bonds because of their higher yield and shorter duration, dealers said.

"It looks as if players are more interested in five-year bonds which offer a better yield in the secondary market and a shorter duration, around 3.9," said a private bank dealer. "The problem with the 10-year bond is its large size."

Greece is seeking bids for a further 75 billion drachmas each of five- and seven-year bonds with coupons of 9.2 percent and 8.9 percent respectively, and 120 billion drachmas of 8.8 percent, 10-year bonds.
The five- and seven-year bonds were auctioned for the first time ever on March 19 and then bids were re-opened on June 17. The 10-year bonds were auctioned for the first time ever on June 17.
Greece will also auction 150 billion drachmas of seven-year floating rate notes on July 29.
The mark was quoted at 156.80/85 drachmas from Monday's 156.780 fix, the dollar at 280.23/33 drachmas from 281.270 and the ecu at 309.53/63 from 309.52 drachmas.

"Ecu/drachma is flat around 309.50 and mark/drachma is trading higher around 156.85 on a softer ecu/mark from 156.65 at open," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "All eyes are on $/mark which came off highs after a statement from the German finance minister."
